contexts.text: That the state of his life would be miserable. Signified. AC 270.
Misery thence. Signified.
Those who thrust themselves down into miseries (ascetically)...
No mercy, is described by, they have not strengthened the hand of the miserable and needy ().
The miserable (a class of the good).
My misery () = temptations.
Lamenting that now they lead a miserable life, because they had imbued these things without any use.
Those who are constituted in miseries; that is, those who are in temptations; for these are in miseries, and are principally meant by the miserable in the Word.
Charity is affected with mercy towards those who are in miseries.
The Divine love is mercy, because all the human race is constituted in miseries.
As with those who are in misfortunes, miseries, and diseases, the loves of self and the world are removed...
(It is not necessary to make ourselves miserable.)
Truth is falsified when it is said that no one can enter into Heaven except him who is miserable and poor... and who reduces himself into miseries.
Man is in a state of misery, because, from himself, he is wholly in evil, and in Hell.
Miserable () = without truths implanted in the life; thus without good.
The voice of a miserable cry do I hear () = their interior state lamentable.
They are vile slaves in Hell; in contempt and misery.
Whence, instead of wealth, they have misery.

And miserable and poor () = that they are without truths and goods. By the miserable and poor, in the spiritual sense of the Word, are meant those who are without the Knowledges of truth and good; for these are spiritually miserable and poor. Illustrated.
By the miserable, and the poor, are chiefly meant those who are not in the Knowledges of truth and good, and yet long for them...
On those who suppose that true Christians must by all means suffer miseries. Explained. SE 1286. SE 1325.

a. By the miserable and the poor are meant those who are spiritually miserable and poor... and thus also those who suffer persecutions from those things which are false and evil, and who endure them, as in temptations; thus who fight against the crew of devils.
A certain miserable wheel driven by water.
They are in a state almost miserable.

He who is in the falsities of evil and the evils of falsity (there) dwells miserably, is clothed miserably, and is led miserably; and will live with such in Hell who had been wicked; thus continually in misery.
The miserable, in general, are all the poor, and also the sojourners and the bound. While the poor regard truths; the miserable regard goods.
And miserable and poor () = that neither do they know that they have not the Knowledges of truth, nor the Knowledges of good...
Spiritual misery and poverty is nothing else than a defect of the Knowledges of truth and good; for a Spirit is then miserable and poor.
By the miserable, in the Word, are meant those who are not in truths because not in the Knowledges of them. Illustrated. AE 238:5.
By the miserable () are here meant those who are in temptations in the world.
By the miserable () are meant those who are being infested by falsities, and are thence in anxiety, and are awaiting deliverance.
By the life of the miserable () is signified the spiritual life oppressed by evils and falsities.

In her shall the miserable of the people hope () = that with those who are not wise from themselves, and who overcome in temptations against these falsities, there shall be intelligence and salvation.
They are reduced into miseries.
